Bash commands and MCP database tools alike; MCP targets are classified from enforce/mcp-database-targets.txt, unlisted targets ask
gh api DELETE and curl-to-interpreter forms that prefix globs cannot express
fixture: tests/secret-scan.test.sh (pattern-deny slice)

detection, not prevention: a PostToolUse hook cannot rewrite or remove the result it reacts to, so the raw output has already reached the context and the transcript. This enforcer reports the exposure and warns; hook:secret-scan is the entry that prevents. Fixture: tests/redact-output.test.sh
blocks gh auth token and keychain readout before the value reaches stdout
fixture: tests/credential-mutation-guard.test.sh (mutation slice of secret-scan.sh; no hook of that name exists)

credential-shaped literals (URI userinfo password, password/secret/token assignment with a literal) in Bash argv, Write content, or Edit new_string; placeholder shapes pass; fixture: tests/secret-scan.test.sh; tree closure (every tracked file through the hook): tests/credential-shape-scan.test.sh

fail-closed pre-push run of the Semgrep security rule pack (enforce/semgrep/) over every whole changed code file; denies on any finding, Semgrep error, skipped or unscanned path, unparseable file, or unresolvable base; fixtures: enforce/tests/push-semgrep-gate.test.sh, enforce/tests/semgrep-rule-pack.test.sh, enforce/tests/r109-rule-text.test.sh, enforce/tests/r109-rule-text-2.test.sh

the reusable .github/workflows/security.yml, pinned by SHA from each adopting repository: runs the security rule pack plus Semgrep p/default over every file a PR adds or modifies (every tracked file on other events), reading no exclude list, and fails closed on a failed listing, a crashed or partial scan, or unreadable JSON; runs CodeQL over languages derived from the tracked files, blocking through GitHub's CodeQL code-scanning check; fixtures: enforce/tests/security-ci-targets.test.sh, enforce/tests/security-ci-semgrep.test.sh, enforce/tests/security-ci-codeql-languages.test.sh, enforce/tests/security-ci-workflow.test.sh (IAN-381 Part 7)

risk classification (IAN-521, 2026-10-01): a slice or PR is high-risk when its diff touches auth, sessions, cookies, CORS/CSP/security headers, rate limits, trust-boundary input validation, SQL construction, secret handling, redaction or PII handling, money, or concurrency, or when the R-109 security-surface detector flags its range; Gate 1 records a Risk line per slice and asks one owner tile per fuzzy control. Nothing mechanical enforces the classification yet: extending the security-surface detector to read the Risk line and the non-security areas, and verifying at merge time that a high-risk slice ran the triad, are deferred. The enforcer name is not a hook: enforce/tests/r110-rule-text.test.sh pins the rule text across CLAUDE.md, the rulebook, and the skills so the wording cannot drift silently

blocks core.hooksPath writes in any spelling, and overrides through -c, --config-env, GIT_CONFIG_KEY_n, GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS, includes, and another config file (GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL, HOME); the drift check only reports after the fact

hash manifest over hooks/, the two fixture suites, and enforce configs; regenerate with --update. hooks/tests/hook-integrity-check.test.sh covers the guard behaviour (drift, absent manifest, --update floors); enforce/tests/hook-hashes-closure.test.sh covers the committed manifest being closed in both directions, which is what CI fails on

blocks hooks-directory tampering, gh alias rule evasion, and the common git-hook skips on a bash-style parse of the command (hooks/shell-command-segments.py): --no-verify in any accepted spelling, commit and am -n, hook-manager variables (HUSKY=0, SKIP, LEFTHOOK=0), config includes, hook-skipping aliases, a git shell function, and deleting, disabling, or overwriting files under .git/hooks; enforce/tests/hook-bypass-guard.test.sh covers the skip forms. Not complete against a determined shell; IAN-155 adds a spelling-independent backstop

PreToolUse Bash git commit: a fix-family subject with no staged test file gets non-blocking additionalContext naming the R-403 path; a warning since IAN-568, never a deny. Fixture: hooks/tests/fix-commit-requires-test.test.sh

PreToolUse on the active tracker's create/update tool (exact names from ~/.claude/TICKET-TRACKER.json): denies a save whose state is the status the config maps specced and planned onto, or the unstarted state type, unless addLabels or labels in the same call carries the specced or planned label; silent without a tracker config and on every other state. A state passed as a raw UUID is not classified. Linear UI moves are outside any hook and are reported by the weekday linear-todo-sweep scheduled task (IAN-473). Fixture: enforce/tests/linear-todo-label-gate.test.sh

asks before any MCP call whose action names a mutating or transmitting verb; browser server exempt, and the Linear server exempt for the write class alone (that server only, not every tracker the ticket skill supports) (merge, submit, upload, apply still ask, as do the destroy and transmit classes on every server)
denies writing a skipped or exclusive test (items 8 and 9)
items 1 and 5 in test trees: a mock of the module the test is named for, and a repository test mocking the pool
item 3 in test trees: a test whose only expect() matchers are mock-call matchers; items 2, 4, 6, 7 stay with the slice critic and the judge
denies TLS, CORS, CSP, CSRF, and bcrypt-cost weakening outside test trees
denies a relative import whose ../ chain resolves above the git toplevel
asks before gh pr merge and before a push whose target branch resolves to main/master; ~/.claude exempt
denies gh pr merge --merge/-m, and --rebase/-r unless gh pr view shows the bundle label and a distinct Refs: trailer on every commit (fail-closed on gh error, timeout, cd, or GH_REPO)

denies every gh pr merge whose PR body (gh pr view --json labels,commits,body,headRefName,headRefOid,isCrossRepository,url, one call; labels and commits must parse too) lacks a Markdown heading starting with Codex review followed by at least one non-blank line outside a fenced code block, or whose section under that heading lacks a reviewer, a model, or a range line with a value, or whose range line holds no <base>..<head> expression whose head endpoint prefixes the headRefOid the same call returned (a stale range, a head in the base position, a bare object name, or a gh that reports no head commit all deny), or whose body holds more than one Codex review heading, unless the PR is trivial tier: an untracked .claude/task-tier.json at the checkout's top records tier trivial for the PR's headRefName, the PR's url names the checkout's origin repository, and isCrossRepository is false (a trivial marker in the PR body is never read); fail-closed on gh error, timeout, cd, or GH_REPO, on a command that runs more than one merge, and on any merge the hook cannot parse. Merges are found by the quote-aware shell scan in hooks/shell-command-tokens.sh (braces, subshells, backticks, control flow, eval and sh -c strings, heredocs fed to a shell, wrappers, quoting, and escapes are all seen; a shell reading its script from stdin and a gh, pr, or merge word built by expansion count as unreadable merges; a mention inside a quoted argument or a heredoc fed to anything but a shell is not a merge), and only a bare gh pr merge on its own simple command is parseable; its flags are read from the scanned words. Fenced code, indented code, and HTML comments do not count as the section. Running the review, and fixing or answering each finding, stay manual. Fixture: enforce/tests/git-workflow-guard.test.sh; build-fast (IAN-401): enforce/tests/build-fast-composition.test.sh pins that a lane or merge mode on the ledger changes no merge-guard decision, enforce/tests/build-fast-rule-text.test.sh pins the R-211, R-514, and R-517 build-fast clauses, and enforce/tests/build-lane.test.sh covers the skills/build-fast lane classifier. IAN-521 (2026-10-01): the reviewer runs on sonnet for every PR outside build-fast, security-touching ones included, and a PR gets at most two review rounds, after which LOW findings are ticketed and answered with the key; the hook does not parse review rounds or the reviewer model, so both stay manual (deferred)
commit-time warning at 5+ files across 3+ directories on main
commit-time warning when a commit adds a route, handler, page, feature slice, or setup file and stages no README
SessionStart warning when another live session holds the same working tree
ConfigChange: refuses a user settings.json that drops a manifest-required hook or does not parse

PostToolUse Bash git push: after a successful push of a non-default branch that has never had a PR (open, merged, or closed; a merged or closed one gets a one-line note naming it), opens a draft with gh pr create --draft (title from the oldest commit, body of subjects, Refs lines, and attribution) and emits the PR monitor instruction; R-605 is applied through the shared pr-range-checks.sh, so a range with no Refs line outside the docs-only and trivial exemptions opens nothing and names /ticket-lifecycle; .enforce.json autoDraftPr false opts out; every error exits 0 with at most a one-line note. Fixture: hooks/tests/draft-pr-on-first-push.test.sh

PostToolUse Bash gh pr create: after a successful create (a PR URL on stdout), emits the instruction to call mcp__ccd_pr__set_monitor with auto_fix, address_comments, and auto_archive_on_close, and never mcp__ccd_pr__set_auto_merge unasked; the call itself stays with the session. Fixture: hooks/tests/pr-monitor-reminder.test.sh

Nuxt packages (nuxt dependency) root the walk at app/ and server/, so abbreviations there warn too; a warning since IAN-568, never a deny

silent in the build-fast fast lane through hooks/build-lane-quiet.sh (IAN-401), fixture enforce/tests/build-lane-quiet.test.sh

artifact marker written with no Dockerfile up to the repo root; Dockerfile with no .dockerignore, no USER, or an unpinned FROM; silent in the build-fast fast lane through hooks/build-lane-quiet.sh (IAN-401), fixture enforce/tests/build-lane-quiet.test.sh

a data-access call (the pool query, any .query, or a function imported from repositories/, database/, or db/) in a loop body, a for/while test or update clause, or an array iteration callback including Promise.all(xs.map(...)); server trees plus every src/services tree; a helper declared elsewhere is not followed, which the query-budget test in CLAUDE-DATABASE.md covers. Fixture: enforce/tests/data-access-rules.test.sh

inside a withTransaction callback: a data-access call that neither runs on nor receives the client, a callback with no client parameter, and a fetch or clients/ call; whether a group of writes needed a transaction stays manual. Fixture: enforce/tests/data-access-rules.test.sh

Python analog via enforce/data-access/python_data_access.py (stdlib ast, run by push-ruff-gate on added lines): repository/db-imported call or execute/scalar(s)/stream call inside a for/async for/while body or while test, a comprehension element or filter, or a map/filter lambda; helpers not followed; suppressed by # data-access-allow: <reason>. Fixture: enforce/tests/data-access-python.test.sh

Python analog via enforce/data-access/python_data_access.py: inside with/async with <expr>.begin()/begin_nested(), an httpx/requests/aiohttp or clients/ call, or a data-access call not given the transaction connection (the as-name or begin receiver, engines excluded); get_connection dependency not inspected. Fixture: enforce/tests/data-access-python.test.sh
decides the intent half the eslint row cannot: two or more writes that must land together issued outside one transaction
a value read, changed in application code, and written back with no SQL guard, FOR UPDATE, or version check
a list query with no LIMIT or an uncapped caller limit, an ORDER BY with no unique tiebreaker, rows loaded to count or sum in memory
a value interpolated into SQL text, or an identifier taken from caller input without a constant allowlist
codex CLI invocation with an OPENAI_API_KEY in scope, a --with-api-key/--with-access-token relogin, or a live login status that is not ChatGPT
verb+noun against enforce/lexicon.json; active only in repos declaring a naming key in .enforce.json
the decidable half only (plural collections, bare adjectives); same opt-in as R-316
decides the 'never destructure a method off its object' half, which is a type question the AST rule deliberately excludes; the eslint row decides the 2+ property reads

PreToolUse Bash: denies a non-conventional subject or more than two triage IDs in the scope; judges only the subject line, so a heredoc message (-F - <<EOF or -m "$(cat <<EOF ...)") whose body holds expansions passes on a conventional subject (IAN-568); asks only when the subject starts with a substitution or expansion it cannot read. The R-506 body ask and the R-214 out-of-scope refusal were removed in IAN-568. Fixtures: enforce/tests/commit-message-guard*.test.sh

SessionStart, every source: records the start timestamp (first valid transcript timestamp, else the hook clock on startup or clear with no transcript file yet) write-once to ~/.claude/projects/<key>/session-start.<session-id> and injects it; ticket-lifecycle open reads started_at from it. Needs transcript_path in the payload; the Cursor adapter passes a synthetic one keyed on the workspace and conversation_id, so a Cursor conversation records the hook clock once. The percentage announcements and elapsed-time reports stay manual. Fixture: hooks/tests/session-start-timestamp.test.sh
crash-safe live task-state tracking on TaskCreate/TaskUpdate; the generated handoff Task state section is rendered by session-end.sh from this hook's output

PreToolUse Bash gh pr create: denies when no commit in the pull request's range (base from --base, else origin's default branch) and no --body or --body-file text carries a `Refs: <KEY>` line; exempts a docs-only range and a trivial tier recorded for the current branch in .claude/task-tier.json; with ~/.claude/TICKET-TRACKER.json absent it allows with a warning naming the degraded path. Ticket opening, advancing, and the key on specs and handoffs stay manual. Fixture: enforce/tests/pr-ticket-ref-gate.test.sh
PreModelSwitch systemMessage on any switch up the price ladder; silent on lateral, downward, or unrankable model ids
design doc written without a Domain vocabulary glossary, an Acceptance criteria section, or a Non-goals section; template in prompts/spec-template.md

asks when package.json, pyproject.toml, go.mod, or a Gemfile gains a dependency name it did not have on disk; version changes, removals, lockfiles, and indirect go requires are silent; parsing in hooks/dependency-add-scan.py, fails open

enforce/doc-sha-reachability.sh: every backticked 7-to-40 hex token, either case and normalised to lowercase, in docs/ and claude/docs/ that resolves to a commit here must be reachable from some ref, reported as DOC-SHA-UNREACHABLE with the citing file and line; a token that resolves to nothing is never a finding, since documents cite other repositories; resolution is one git cat-file --batch-check over all tokens and one git rev-list --all, never a process per token (IAN-183); the escape hatch is an unreachable-sha HTML comment naming the same SHA on the same line with a reason holding a real word, outside inline code, fences and enclosing comments, one marker per citation; every state it cannot judge (shallow clone, unreadable document, failed resolver, unlistable change set) exits 2 rather than reporting success; hooks/pre-push.sample runs --push, which reads the pre-push ref list on stdin and inspects the pushed commits rather than the working tree, and aborts on exit 2 as well as 1; the push half is inert until install-git-hooks.sh is re-run in a repository, since git hooks are not version-controlled; fixture enforce/tests/doc-sha-reachability.test.sh carries the IAN-260 spec and its three keep/ tags as the live regression case; the historical corpus is reported by --all and is not gated (IAN-308 phase 1, IAN-322)
compound naming: base noun first; judged against the project Domain vocabulary glossary, and dropped from the judged set when a repository has none
Stop and SubagentStop gate; runs the project's discovered test/typecheck commands when the tree is dirty, fails open when none is discoverable, skips non-writing subagent roles

denies writes to the gate inputs and, once a slice is red, to every test tree and locked fixture or spec path; Bash covered by its parsed write targets (redirections, tee, mutating-verb operands, cp-family destinations, nested shells, inline-script write calls) with quoted text and heredoc bodies set aside; tdd.sh amend opens a one-file window for the slice author; runner configs and package.json test scripts ask
role boundaries by the agent_type hook field against enforce/role-policy.json; no restriction when the field is absent or the role is unlisted

phase from .claude/tdd-lock.json written by enforce/tdd.sh: open denies production writes, red and green deny test writes, amending allows only the amended test; tdd.sh abandon closes a stale lock whose tests are committed and passing; opening the slice is the manual step
the dispatch half of R-412: everything after tdd.sh open is the same lock and guard; opening the slice and committing between RED and GREEN stay manual
